title: St Pauls Carnival
text: Begun in 1968 as the St Pauls Festival, to improve relations between the area's European, African, Caribbean and Asian residents and to challenge negative stereotypes. Early on, residents sold home-cooked food from their front gardens. Held on the first Saturday in July, with a masquerade procession, steel bands, sound systems and food stalls; a reported 70,000 people came in 2008.

title: Mas camps and steel bands
text: From 1979 Trinidadian Francis Salandy chaired the carnival, bringing Trinidadian-style mas camps, where the costumes are made, and keeping the tradition of steel bands. Themes included 'Survival' (1979), 'Resistance' (1980) and 'Not Guilty' (1981). It became the St Pauls Afrikan-Caribbean Carnival in 1991.

title: Carnival through the years
text: Cancelled in 2002 and 2006, it returned in 2007, the 200th anniversary of the Slave Trade Act. After a gap from 2015 to 2017 it returned in 2018 with Arts Council funding, and went online in 2020 during COVID-19.

title: St Agnes' Church
text: The first carnival was organised by local committees with help from the vicar of St Agnes Church and Carmen Beckford.
check: Pin placed at St Agnes Park, near the church.
